title: Interop EASE — Migration Demo: Switch from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood
summary: Short demo focused on parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API. Covered API mapping, streaming/function-calls differences, embeddings parity, cost/latency tradeoffs, dedicated vs private deployment decision factors, and next steps for a 2-week pilot + benchmark. Customer emphasized data residency and SSO + KMS for private deployment. Action items assigned for benchmark plan and security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining from redwood side, we have priya and liam and bea — glad to walk through the migration map today
[00:05] Maya Chen: thanks jordan, we wanted a very concrete plan — our main ask is parity with our current openai+anthropic mix and minimal changes to infra
[00:18] Roberto Diaz: yeah i can share a quick context — we run a mixture of gpt and together models, most of our endpoints use streaming for interactive features, and embeddings for search. latency around 200-300ms p50 now, cost is creeping up
[00:34] Priya Suresh: okay great, we'll start with the API surface. Redwood's text/generate maps to the standard patterns but there are a few param names to watch, and streaming is supported but has a slightly different chunk framing sometimes
[00:46] Hannah Park: when you say different framing, do we need to change our streaming parser?
[00:52] Priya Suresh: maybe small tweak, sometimes the delta tokens events include extra metadata field names — i've seen teams reuse their existing parser with a two-line change, i'll paste a snippet after the call
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: also note function/tool calling is supported. the big difference is Redwood exposes a model variant aliasing layer so you can route to smaller quantized variants automatically — helpful for cost
[01:20] Roberto Diaz: okay that routing layer sounds interesting. how does fallback work if the variant lacks a capability? e.g. function calling with structured responses?
[01:29] Bea Navarro: good question — we have automatic fallback policies in the routing config. you can set priority: latency first, cost first, or strict capability match. if a variant lacks a capability we fall back to the next compatible variant or region
[01:44] Maya Chen: about embeddings: we use ada-like embeddings from openai and a separate service for nearest-neighbors. how close is crimson/other redwood embeddings? (note: customer mis-said model name here)
[01:58] Priya Suresh: we publish similarity tests — most customers see 95%+ recall parity on their evaluation sets after a quick calibration. there may be small drift with together-style models; we recommend running a 48-72 hour embedding parity check with your sample queries
[02:13] Hannah Park: security — we need SOC2 type 2, SSO via our IDP (okta), audit logs, and KMS for key management. is that supported in private?
[02:25] Jordan Lee: yes SOC2 and enterprise compliance packages are available. Private (VPC) installs support customer KMS/HSM integrations and SAML/SSO. audit logs are part of our console — retention varies by plan but we can align with your retention reqs
[02:40] Samir Patel: can we see a sample audit log schema? we need to show it to auditors
[02:45] Jordan Lee: absolutely — i'll drop the security pack and a sample schema (link) after the call.
[02:52] Roberto Diaz: for the pilot we'd like to run a three-way run: baseline on openai/anthropic/together, run on redwood hosted, and on redwood private instance — compare latency/cost/quality
[03:04] Liam O'Connor: perfect. typical pilot plan is 10-14 days with scripted prompt set, matching traffic profile. we can help run the benchmarks and provide a report with token-level cost breakdowns
[03:17] Maya Chen: timeline — we need something that shows quick wins in 2 weeks for execs. can we have a minimal pilot that doesn't require a full private deployment?
[03:27] Priya Suresh: yes, start hosted with dataset-only privacy controls, then move to dedicated or private if you need KMS/air-gap. we recommend starting hosted to validate parity fast, then enable VPC in the second phase
[03:39] Roberto Diaz: about tokenization — we use tokenization heuristics tuned to our prompts, will that change output lengths/cost?
[03:45] Bea Navarro: there can be minor tokenization diffs across model families. our optimize tool will analyze prompt-token ratios and suggest small rewrites or caching to reduce unit costs
[03:56] Hannah Park: any flags we should watch for when migrating code? specific param renames or error codes?
[04:02] Priya Suresh: yes, parameter mapping doc is our key artifact — e.g., openai's max_tokens ~ redwood's max_output_tokens, temperature maps same, but stop sequences handling and n-best behavior has slight differences. also error codes for rate-limit vs model-unavailable are different ids, we include a translation table in the migration guide
[04:22] Jordan Lee: i want to demo a quick mapping for a streaming chat sample — bear with me, i'll share my screen
[04:30] [screen share noise]
[04:34] Priya Suresh: here's a sample curl from your current openai call and the equivalent redwood curl. you can see we keep the messages array identical, just swap endpoint and a couple of param names
[04:50] Roberto Diaz: that looks straightforward, any gotchas for multipart messages or function metadata?
[04:55] Priya Suresh: function metadata should be included in the new call as well, but if you rely on some specific together schema you might need to map field names. we have a small shim library in our SDKs that does that translation for node/python/rust
[05:12] Maya Chen: sdk support — do you have feature parity in official sdks? we primarily use python and go
[05:18] Bea Navarro: python is first-class, go SDK is stable and used by several customers, and we have a community maintained minimal rust client. SDKs implement streaming, embeddings, and function calling parity helpers
[05:30] Samir Patel: for private deployment: network diagram and cert rotations, who's responsible?
[05:36] Liam O'Connor: for VPC we provide the private control plane and deployment artifacts; certs and KMS keys are customer-managed. we support automatic cert rotation helpers but customer ops owns keys and network peering
[05:48] Roberto Diaz: curious about model variants — what are the quantization tradeoffs, do we lose generation quality?
[05:54] Priya Suresh: quantized variants are tuned for minimal quality loss. in many classification/rerank workloads we see parity within margin. for open-ended generation it's model and prompt dependent; that's why we run evals on your prompts and compare perplexity/ROUGE/embedding-similarity as metrics
[06:12] Maya Chen: ok, cost — you mentioned routing rules can save cost. can you give an example?
[06:18] Liam O'Connor: one simple pattern: route NLU classification traffic to a small quantized variant, route long-form creative generation to a full fp model. you can set thresholds so under heavy load we fall back to a cheaper region or variant to preserve throughput
[06:30] Roberto Diaz: do we get token-level cost breakdowns in the console during the pilot?
[06:36] Jordan Lee: yes, the console shows token-level cost, per-route breakdowns, and latency percentiles. we'll give you a dashboard access for the pilot
[06:44] Maya Chen: okay can you walk through the proposed pilot steps?
[06:47] Liam O'Connor: step 1: share prompt set and dataset, step 2: Redwood runs hosted parity test (48 hrs), step 3: deploy dedicated/private for second run if needed (3-5 days setup), step 4: joint review of metrics and decision
[06:59] Roberto Diaz: dependencies? we need SSO access for console and a service account for benchmark runs
[07:04] Jordan Lee: we'll request an okta SAML assertion and create a service account with restricted tokens. we'll also provide temporary credentials for the hosted pilot runs
[07:14] Samir Patel: what about data retention during pilot? we have to ensure logs are purged after 30 days
[07:19] Bea Navarro: retention is configurable. for pilots we can set a 30-day retention and audit that config
[07:25] Hannah Park: any examples where migration caused regression in hallucination for certain prompts? how do you test for that?
[07:31] Priya Suresh: we run targeted evals with user prompts and compare redwood outputs vs baseline using automated metrics and manual spot checks. if we see regressions we tune model selection or prompt rewrites. the optimize tool can suggest small prompt changes and show cost/quality delta
[07:48] Maya Chen: ok this is helpful. next steps?
[07:52] Jordan Lee: recap: jordan will send migration guide, param mapping table, security pack, and a pilot plan spreadsheet. liam and priya will prepare the pilot dashboard and a cost estimate. bea will coordinate SDK snippets and small shim libs
[08:06] Roberto Diaz: can we get a target date for kickoff? we aim for week of april 6th
[08:11] Jordan Lee: that works — we'll aim to have the pilot materials in your folder by march 25th so you can review before april 6th start
[08:19] Maya Chen: perfect. thanks team
[08:22] [crosstalk] Hannah Park: thanks jordan, talk soon
[08:26] [end call]
